The core issue lies in the misalignment between forecast confidence and actual outcome resolution. The model exhibits high uncertainty (UNC=0.2495) and near-zero resolution (RES=0.0027), indicating it fails to distinguish outcomes beyond chance. This suggests either weak features or an inherently unpredictable target. The reliability component (REL=0.0048) is also minimal, reinforcing that the model does not improve upon baseline performance. The diagnostic approach recommends evaluating whether the model is overfitting or lacks signal. The proposed solution involves shifting focus from calibration tuning to feature diagnostics when RES is negligible. Adaptive thresholds based on resolution ensure gates respond to model competence rather than static criteria. The ultimate fallback is to return base rate predictions with uncertainty bands, reflecting honest epistemic limits.
